title: Token Factory 101
focus:
Audience: a software engineer in their first week on Nebius Token Factory. They know vLLM, SGLang, KV cache, Kubernetes, Helm and GitLab. Target length about 30 minutes: cover every section below fully, but tell no extended analogies and no dramatised stories. Be thorough but plain: no extended analogies, no war-story drama. Use ONLY facts in the three sources; if a source doesn't say why something is the way it is, don't explain why.

Cover in this order:
1. Product (about 4 min): formerly AI Studio; serverless per-token with base and fast flavors; dedicated endpoints per GPU-hour; custom weights/BYOW with artifact kinds full, lora, drafter; post-training; playground; routing keys; control vs data plane; templates and flavors.
2. One dedicated endpoint from UI to pods (about 5 min): nebo UI (NestJS BFF + React) -> CPL inference-backend and its spec database -> model-weights API and worker (the worker validates the uploaded weights' config.json against the base model; a 12.8 GiB weights ZIP went from upload to artifact-ready in about 2 minutes; this is weights ingest, NOT deploying an endpoint) and templates -> endpoints-controller's four modes -> Argo Application -> the "vllm" chart that renders vLLM, SGLang and TRT-LLM -> KAI scheduler, with the 4-GPU gotcha told briefly.
3. One inference request (about 4 min): ingress -> DPL (model list, exact-match lookup, rate limits, logs, billing metadata) -> inference-router with kv-indexer -> engine-proxy -> engine. Billing: per-token path vs de-billing-watcher from pod events. cryod for cold start and its snapshot hash.
4. Repos (about 4 min): walk through the ai-studio-service layout folder by folder (go/ services; inference_playground/backend/app = the CPL/DPL monolith vs backend/apps = separately released services such as model-weights-api vs backend/packages = shared libraries; infra/deploy = one deploy module per component plus environment overlays; schemas/s2s contracts); nebo; engine forks; Elastic's repo.
5. Teams (about 8 min, the core of the episode): for EACH of tf-endpoints, tf-cpl, tf-dpl, tf-billing-dev, tf-orchestra, tf-aai, tf-platform, tokenfactory-fe, tokenfactory-ft, tf-elastic, plus solution architects, IAM and product: the duty handle, what it owns in code, and the people the source names. Explain streams, CODEOWNERS sections, "ToFa developers" fallback, self-ship paths, @duty in #tokenfactory-support with the MR link, the "What team should I call" canvas.
6. Process (about 4 min): Jira TOFA/AIBE/AIFE; PRD with release stages 0-3 -> EDR -> merge requests; the EDR conventions from the source (header table, problem/goals/solution, existing-model recap, rejected alternatives kept visible, API and data-model tables, iterations, out of scope) and what reviewers ask; one owning team per MR; users/<name>/ branches and "TICKET-ID colon description" commits.
7. Local development (about 2 min): the official CPL/DPL + docker-compose Postgres/Redis + OpenAI stub on 8000 pattern; Elastic's bigger local stack and what it was used for.
8. A glossary of 10-15 terms (about 3 min), then a first-week recap of 4-6 concrete steps drawn from the sources (run the local CPL/DPL with the stub, read the Speculators Management EDR, find your team's duty handle and CODEOWNERS section, make an example change to testing with your buddy). End plainly.

Exact facts to get right (take 1 got these wrong):
- de-billing-watcher has its OWN approver group (Ihar Loban and Yuriy Natarov). Do not say tf-billing-dev owns or maintains it.
- Token Factory IAM roles live in nebo iam/metadata/studio and the IAM team approves them; nebo tokenfactory/ holds ModelHub, the Argo workflow renderer, an older endpoints-controller copy and de-billing-watcher.
- nebius/golden is the production branch of the SGLang fork; don't generalise it to every fork.
- Elastic's local stack was used for custom weights, BYOT and LoRA demos; its "local driver" stood in for endpoints-controller plus the Helm chart. It was not a cryod test rig. Don't say what language the driver is in.
- The README says "make an example change to testing; ask your buddy". Self-ship paths are a separate CODEOWNERS fact.
- Do not add details the sources don't contain: no TLS, no "sidecar", no TCP, no "sits on the control plane", no price multiplication, no reasons why the chart is named vllm, no hypothetical EDR examples, no claims about which team blocks the most MRs, no rules about DMs.
- inference-backend and inference-data-plane are deployments (processes), not repositories; both run code from ai-studio-service.
- Mark inferred ownership as "from commit history".
- Hosts must not read the notes aloud or refer to "the source notes".
- LoRA gets one sentence only (separate episode).
- No hype or futurism. Do not end with metaphors about money or liquid gold.
review_notes:
# Episode 46 "Token Factory 101": review log

Sources: src1-product-and-architecture.md, src2-teams-and-ownership.md, src3-process-localdev-glossary.md (curated from
internal notes + ai-studio-service/nebo code + public docs; no credentials, IPs or internal URLs). Format deep-dive, length long.

## Take 1 (length long, focus1.txt): 55:42, 40.7 MB. REJECTED
Structure and coverage were good (all 10 focus items present, names correct, LoRA one sentence). Problems:
- Too long: 55:42 vs 25-35 min target. Long analogies (restaurant/hostess for cache-aware routing, "armored car").
- Wrong ownership: said tf-billing-dev maintains de-billing-watcher (source: its own approver group, Ihar Loban + Yuriy Natarov).
- Wrong location: said nebo `tokenfactory/` holds IAM role definitions (source: nebo `iam/metadata/studio/`, approved by the IAM team).
- Over-generalised: "production branch of all forks is nebius/golden, don't deploy off main" (source: SGLang fork's production branch only).
- Wrong framing of the local stack: presented as how Elastic tests cryod GPU snapshots, driver "a Bash script reading local Postgres
  and running docker" (source: demos were custom weights, BYOT, LoRA; driver stands in for endpoints-controller + chart).
- Invented details: TLS termination at ingress; DPL validating token "against the IAM service"; kv-indexer "a sidecar"; engine-proxy
  "manages TCP connections"; de-billing-watcher "sits on the control plane"; is_token_billable "multiplies tokens by SKU rate";
  backstory for why the vllm chart renders SGLang; "blast radius / last known good state" rationale for CPL/DPL; a hypothetical
  "we evaluated Redis, 2 ms" EDR example; cryod "GPU would crash the node"; "orchestra blocks more PRs than anyone".
- Invented rules: "never DM people, cardinal sin", "include the Jira ticket"; README "suggests tweaking testing overlays" (it says
  "make an example change to testing, ask your buddy").
- Garbled stretch ~37:00 (hosts reading notes aloud: "they've noted them here", "I am a file").
- Hype ending: "GPU compute like liquid currency", "routing liquid gold".

## Take 2 (length default, focus2.txt): 20:26, 15.0 MB. REJECTED (too short, gaps, 3 errors)
Fixed from take 1: de-billing-watcher ownership (own group, correctly stated), IAM roles in nebo iam/metadata/studio,
nebius/golden only on the SGLang fork, local stack = custom weights/BYOT/LoRA demos, not a cryod rig; README quote right;
plain ending; no hype; team-by-team names covered well.
Problems:
- 20:26, below the 25-35 min target.
- Missing: ai-studio-service layout (go/, backend app vs apps vs packages, infra/deploy, schemas/s2s), PRD stages, EDR
  conventions (header table, rejected alternatives kept visible), real glossary (3 terms only), first-week recap.
- Error: intro frames "12.8 GiB from POST to ready in 2 min" as deploying a model; it was the weights artifact ingest
  (the endpoint itself was ready ~4 min after a 1-GPU recreate).
- Error: "the worker validates the templates" (it validates the uploaded weights: config.json vs base model).
- Error: "CPL lives in the inference-backend repository" (inference-backend is the CPL deployment; code is in ai-studio-service).

## Take 3 (length long, focus3.txt): 22:21, 16.4 MB. PUBLISHED
Full transcript checked against the three source files. Fixed from take 2: 12.8 GiB / ~2 min framed correctly as weights
ingest, not endpoint deploy; worker validates config.json vs base model; inference-backend / inference-data-plane described
as deployments of ai-studio-service code; repo layout walked folder by folder; PRD stages 0-3; EDR conventions; 15-term
glossary; 5-step first-week list. Kept take 2's fixes (de-billing-watcher own approver group, IAM roles in nebo
iam/metadata/studio, nebius/golden only on the SGLang fork, local stack = demos, not a cryod rig). No customer names, no
credentials/hosts/IPs; LoRA is one sentence.
Minor issues left: 22:21 is below the 25-35 min target (long gave 56 min with analogies, default gave 20); intro says
"validate every single layer configuration" (source: config.json vs base); "drop invalid requests instantly" is a small
embellishment; some names are labelled confirmed where the source marks them inferred; tokenfactory-fe and tf-platform get
one or no names; closing line mentions Conway's law (not in sources, harmless).
